summary: Step-by-step broadcast tutorial building an animated 2D lower-third with Motion Design: shapes, Material Designer layers, text actors, Translucent Priority and Grid Arrange modifiers, Sequencer marks for stop/continue, Remote Control controllers with Conditional behaviors, Storm Sync .spak export, and Rundown/Broadcast playout.
gotchas: Experimental feature
Text actor must use Translucent style for Translucent Priority sorting
Translucent materials cannot cast shadows
Rundown/Broadcast section needs a two-monitor setup

summary: Reference for Motion Design Animators (parameter-driven, keyframe-free animation added via the Operator Stack): global magnitude/time source, common numeric properties, linked properties and ranges, the Bounce, Curve, Oscillate, Pulse, Soundwave, Time and Wiggle animators, and the Clock and Counter text animators with format variables and presets.
gotchas: Animators show 'No properties are currently linked to this animator' until a property is linked
Frame Rate property cannot exceed the project/hardware max
Combining Display Format/Pattern with Additive mode gives unpredictable results

summary: Reference for Motion Design Modifiers in the Operator Stack: layout (Align Between, Auto Follow, Grid/Radial Arrange, Justify, Look At, Spline Path), geometry (Bend, Bevel, Boolean, Extrude, Pattern, Plane Cut, Spline Sweep, Subdivide, Taper, Dynamic Mesh Converter), rendering (Material Parameter, Global Opacity, Translucent Priority, Visibility, Mask Layer) and the Transition Logic Sub Layer modifier.
gotchas: Geometry modifiers need Motion Design primitives or a static mesh converted with Dynamic Mesh Converter
Bend and Taper add a Subdivide modifier that cannot be removed
Material Parameter needs a dynamic material instance; masking only works on Translucent or Masked materials
Size to Texture is intended for rectangles only

summary: Reference for the Remote Control API WebSocket server (default ws://127.0.0.1:30020): JSON message format, the http message type that tunnels HTTP routes, preset.register/preset.unregister subscriptions and the PresetFields* events, plus a sample HTML/JS test page.
gotchas: Beta feature; use caution when shipping with it
Default port 30020, changed in Project Settings > Plugins > Remote Control

summary: Hub page for Motion Design (broadcast/motion graphics toolset): links to the Quick Start, Your First Graphic, Cloners and Effectors, Rundown Server, Operator Stack and Scene State pages.
gotchas: Experimental feature

summary: How to launch the editor or an uncooked game from the command line or a shortcut with a .uproject path, the -game and -debug switches, overriding the startup map on the command line or via GameDefaultMap, and in-game console commands such as OPEN and TRAVEL.
gotchas: -debug needs project modules compiled in Debug configuration
Map URL options are appended with ? (e.g. ?Game=)
Page uses older executable names (UEEditor.exe / UE4Editor.exe)

summary: Full guide to TArray in C++: creating and filling (Init, Add vs Emplace, Append, Insert, SetNum), iteration, Sort/HeapSort/StableSort, queries and Find/IndexOfByKey/FindByPredicate, removal including swap variants, copy/move operators, heap functions, slack management, and uninitialized/zeroed raw-memory functions.
gotchas: Invalid index with operator[] or RemoveAt causes a runtime error
Sort and HeapSort are unstable; use StableSort to keep order
GetData pointer is invalid after any mutating operation
Uninitialized/Zeroed functions can create invalid elements for types needing construction

summary: Table of UCLASS specifiers (Abstract, Blueprintable, BlueprintType, Config, EditInlineNew, HideCategories, MinimalAPI, Placeable, Transient, Within, etc.) and class metadata specifiers (BlueprintSpawnableComponent, DisplayName, ChildCanTick, ToolTip, etc.) controlling engine and editor behavior.
gotchas: Metadata only exists in the editor; do not write game logic that reads it
NotBlueprintable is the default unless inherited
Intrinsic and NoExport should not be used on new classes

summary: Guide to TMap and TMultiMap in C++: adding (Add, Emplace, Append), iteration over TPair elements, lookups (operator[], Contains, Find, FindOrAdd, FindRef, FindKey), removal, KeySort/ValueSort, slack (Reserve, Compact, Shrink), and writing custom KeyFuncs.
gotchas: operator[] asserts if the key is missing
Element order is not stable; iteration order may differ from insertion
FindOrAdd can invalidate previously obtained pointers/references
Custom KeyFuncs must keep Matches and GetKeyHash consistent; mutating a key is undefined behavior
